key_insight: ShipNet uses geometric deep learning on hull point clouds to rapidly predict both local pressure and far-field wave patterns from ship geometry and speed.
engineering_relevance: It enables fast design-space exploration for ship hydrodynamics, replacing expensive CFD-like simulations with near real-time surrogate predictions.
method: Dynamic graph convolution on hull point clouds
Multi-head decoder for pressure and wave elevation
Composite loss with point-wise regression and image-structure terms
evidence_signal: Trained on 420 inviscid free-surface simulations from two yacht hull families, ShipNet reached R^2=0.98 for hull pressure and R^2=0.91 for wave fields, with about 0.15 s inference per case.
watch_item: The model is limited to the narrow geometry and speed range in the training data, and it was trained on inviscid potential-flow simulations rather than viscous CFD.
paper_title: ShipNet: A Geometric Deep Learning Surrogate for Real-Time Ship Hydrodynamics
